text: Full-Mouth Dental Implants in McLean & Alexandria, VA

When most or all of your teeth are failing or gone, both arches can be rebuilt on implants: a fixed zirconia bridge on four to eight posts per arch, or a denture that clips onto them. Planned and placed by one board-certified prosthodontist, Dr. Esam Nahlah.
From surgery to the final zirconia

A full-mouth case is planned as one job rather than tooth by tooth. The cone-beam scan maps the bone in both jaws, and the upper and lower teeth are designed together so the bite balances. On this site these cases are called double arch.
Fixed teeth that stay in: screwed down, not taken out at night
Cared for like natural teeth, with six-monthly cleanings
Implants load the jawbone, which a denture resting on the gums cannot do
Zirconia, resistant to decay and to fractures and chips
Designed and milled in the practice's own laboratory
Three ways to replace every tooth.
Your scan, your bone and what you want from the result decide between them.
A removable denture on each arch, clipped onto two or more implants. Around 60% of natural function at a moderate cost, and it comes out for cleaning.
A fixed zirconia bridge on four implants per arch, the rear two tilted toward stronger bone. In most cases you leave surgery with fixed provisional teeth.
Where the bone and the bite call for it, each fixed arch is carried on up to eight implants. Over 98% of natural function, and the highest cost of the three.
Bone loss is often where it starts, not where it ends.

From the first scan to two finished arches.
An examination and a cone-beam scan of both jaws. Pricing, insurance and financing are discussed at this visit, before you commit to anything.
Failing teeth come out and thin bone is built up where the plan needs it. The specialist who removes a tooth is the one who replaces it.
The implants go in at the office under local anesthetic, with nitrous oxide or oral sedation, guided by the scan. With All-on-4, most patients leave wearing fixed provisional teeth.
Three to four months later, once the implants have fused, the final zirconia arches are fitted, shaped and bite-balanced by the specialist who planned them.

What a full mouth costs, and how it is paid.

The number depends on how many implants each arch needs, whether extractions or grafting come first, and whether the teeth are a removable denture or fixed zirconia. It is set at your consultation, once the scan has been read; two quotes for the same mouth can differ by thousands for exactly those reasons.
Most PPO dental plans are accepted, and claims are filed for you. Financing reaches $60,000 with terms of up to 96 months, and a financial coordinator helps you apply.

faq: Who is a candidate for full-mouth dental implants?

Adults whose teeth are mostly missing or failing, and people tired of loose dentures. Many already have enough bone; many of the rest qualify after bone grafting or extractions. The cone-beam scan at the consultation answers it for your mouth.
How many implants does a full mouth need?
Per arch: two or more for a removable implant denture, four for an All-on-4 fixed arch, and up to eight for a fixed bridge on more implants. The scan decides how many your bone will carry.

How long does full-mouth treatment take?

With All-on-4, about three to four months from surgery to the final zirconia arches, then a further two to four months for complete healing around them. Grafting, if you need it, adds several months of healing before the implants go in.
Will I have teeth while the implants heal?
Yes. With All-on-4, in most cases you leave the surgery wearing fixed provisional teeth, which stay in place while the implants fuse.

How do I look after full-mouth implants?
A fixed arch is brushed and flossed like natural teeth and stays in at night. The five-year warranty asks one thing of you: the six-monthly cleanings.

Is sedation available for full-mouth surgery?
Yes: nitrous oxide or oral sedation, given at the office by the practice's own team. The practice does not offer IV sedation or general anesthesia.
